IDE Interface

This document defines the motherboard parallel ATA interface in I/O slot 11. Return to the main page.

Revision 1.0 follows memory map 2.1. One PALCE20V8Q-15JC/4, one CD74HCT164E, two SN74HCT245N bus transceivers, and one SN74HCT244N connect the MC68EC000 bus to a standard 40-pin ATA cable. The adapter implements programmed I/O and meets PIO mode 0 timing. It accepts IORDY wait extension and supports two devices on one cable.

1. Compatibility

The connector and control signals follow the parallel ATA host interface. The BIOS starts each device in its reset transfer mode and uses PIO mode 0. ATA hard disks, solid-state disks, and ATAPI optical drives share the same electrical interface. A passive 44-pin adapter can connect a 2.5-inch drive, and a True IDE adapter can connect a CompactFlash card. A SATA device needs an active PATA-to-SATA bridge.

Both device positions work. Firmware selects device 0 or device 1 with the Device/Head register. Drives may use master/slave jumpers. Cable Select requires a cable that routes pin 28 for that purpose, such as a standard 80-conductor ATA cable. The host timing does not depend on cable detection, so 40-conductor and 80-conductor cables both work at PIO mode 0.

Device capacity, geometry, command set, removable-media status, and logical sector size come from IDENTIFY DEVICE or IDENTIFY PACKET DEVICE. The design fixes no drive model or capacity. Firmware must reject a device whose IDENTIFY data does not report a command path it implements.

2. Architecture

MC68EC000 D15..D0 <-> two HCT245 transceivers <-> ATA DD15..DD0
MC68EC000 A3..A1 --> HCT244 --+---------------> ATA DA2..DA0
                               +--> PAL IDE_A3..IDE_A1
R/W --> two HCT04 inverters --> IDE_RW
IO11_n, A4, IDE_RW, UDS_n, LDS_n --> PALCE20V8 --> ATA controls
MFP_CLK_5 --> HCT164 --> PAL timing taps QB and QD
ATA IORDY ------------------------------------> PAL completion gate
ATA INTRQ --> HCT04 inverter --> level-2 priority input
PAL IDE_DTACK_n ------------------------------> motherboard DTACK tree

IO11_n supplies the protected slot select. The IDE adapter sees supervisor cycles because the top I/O decoder suppresses user cycles before it asserts IO11_n. The motherboard timeout ends a transfer with a bus error if a selected device holds IORDY low for 51.2 microseconds.

3. Register Map

CPU address lines A3..A1 drive ATA DA2..DA0 through U_IDE_BUS. A4 selects the command block or the control block. The command-block data register uses a 16-bit word at an even address. The remaining registers use D7..D0 at odd addresses.

Canonical ATA register addresses
68k address ATA select DA2..DA0 Read Write Width
$F60000 CS0_n 000 Data Data 16-bit word
$F60003 CS0_n 001 Error Features Lower byte
$F60005 CS0_n 010 Sector Count Sector Count Lower byte
$F60007 CS0_n 011 LBA Low LBA Low Lower byte
$F60009 CS0_n 100 LBA Mid LBA Mid Lower byte
$F6000B CS0_n 101 LBA High LBA High Lower byte
$F6000D CS0_n 110 Device Device Lower byte
$F6000F CS0_n 111 Status Command Lower byte
$F6001D CS1_n 110 Alternate Status Device Control Lower byte
$F6001F CS1_n 111 Device Address Reserved Lower byte

The PAL decodes A4..A1 and ignores A16..A5, so the 32-byte register pattern repeats through the slot. Firmware uses the canonical addresses above. A byte access to the data register receives no IDE_DTACK_n and reaches the motherboard timeout. Word accesses to an 8-bit register transfer the lower byte and leave the upper byte undefined.

4. Data Path and Byte Order

U_IDE_DATA_LO connects ATA DD7..DD0 to CPU D7..D0. U_IDE_DATA_HI connects DD15..DD8 to D15..D8. Both parts are SN74HCT245N. Their A ports face ATA, their B ports face the processor, and IDE_RW drives both DIR pins. Two cascaded gates in U_IDE_IRQ buffer processor R/W into IDE_RW. A read drives A to B. A write drives B to A. IDE_BUF_OE_n enables both parts during a valid IDE cycle.

The straight bit mapping preserves ATA register and command-word bit numbers. It places each pair of sector bytes in reverse order in big-endian memory because ATA transfers the first byte on DD7..DD0. BIOS sector reads swap the two bytes in each 16-bit data word before storing them. Sector writes apply the same swap before writing the data register. IDENTIFY numeric words keep their bit positions; firmware handles ATA string fields with their specified byte order.

Place 33 ohm series resistors between each transceiver A-side cable route and the ATA header. The transceivers isolate the processor bus from cable loading. The switched drive-power harness powers the selected drive before firmware accesses this interface.

5. PAL and Timing Control

U_IDE_CTRL is a PALCE20V8Q-15JC/4 in a 28-pin PLCC socket. The CUPL listing below is the source of record for the programmed equations and pin assignment. The PAL uses combinational mode. Pin 17 reads the reset-stretcher output. Pin 27 is an unused input and connects to ground.

PALCE20V8 PLCC assignment
Pins Signals Use
2, 3, 4, 5, 6 IO11_n, IDE_A1, IDE_A2, IDE_A3, A4 Slot and register decode
7, 9, 10 IDE_RW, UDS_n, LDS_n Direction and transfer width
11, 12, 13 IDE_QB, IDE_QD, IDE_IORDY Strobe and completion timing
16, 17 PERIPH_RESET_n, IDE_RESET_PULSE_n Cycle inhibit and stretched drive reset
18, 19, 20, 21 IDE_CYCLE, IDE_CS0_n, IDE_CS1_n, IDE_DIOR_n Cycle and read controls
23, 24, 25, 26 IDE_DIOW_n, IDE_DTACK_n, IDE_BUF_OE_n, IDE_RESET_n Write, completion, buffers, reset
1, 8, 15, 22 No connection PLCC package no-connect pins
14, 28 Ground, +5 V Supply; 100 nF bypass at the socket

Complete CUPL Source

Name     IDE_CONTROL;
PartNo   001;
Date     2026-09-12;
Revision 01;
Designer m68k-computer;
Company  None;
Assembly None;
Location U_IDE_CTRL;
Device   g20v8;

/* CUPL uses 24-pin logical numbers. The fitter maps them to PLCC pins. */

PIN 1  = IO11_n;
PIN 2  = IDE_A1;
PIN 3  = IDE_A2;
PIN 4  = IDE_A3;
PIN 5  = A4;
PIN 6  = IDE_RW;
PIN 7  = UDS_n;
PIN 8  = LDS_n;
PIN 9  = IDE_QB;
PIN 10 = IDE_QD;
PIN 11 = IDE_IORDY;
PIN 13 = PERIPH_RESET_n;
PIN 14 = IDE_RESET_PULSE_n;
PIN 23 = NC_I13;

PIN 15 = IDE_CYCLE;
PIN 16 = IDE_CS0_n;
PIN 17 = IDE_CS1_n;
PIN 18 = IDE_DIOR_n;
PIN 19 = IDE_DIOW_n;
PIN 20 = IDE_DTACK_n;
PIN 21 = IDE_BUF_OE_n;
PIN 22 = IDE_RESET_n;

DATA_REG = !A4 & !IDE_A3 & !IDE_A2 & !IDE_A1;
BYTE_CYCLE = !LDS_n;
WORD_CYCLE = !UDS_n & !LDS_n;

IDE_CYCLE = !IO11_n & PERIPH_RESET_n & IDE_RESET_PULSE_n
          & ((!DATA_REG & BYTE_CYCLE) # (DATA_REG & WORD_CYCLE));

IDE_CS0_n = !(IDE_CYCLE & !A4);
IDE_CS1_n = !(IDE_CYCLE & A4);

IDE_DIOR_n = !(IDE_CYCLE & IDE_QB & IDE_RW);
IDE_DIOW_n = !(IDE_CYCLE & IDE_QB & !IDE_RW);

IDE_DTACK_n = !(IDE_CYCLE & IDE_QD & IDE_IORDY);
IDE_BUF_OE_n = !IDE_CYCLE;
IDE_RESET_n = PERIPH_RESET_n & IDE_RESET_PULSE_n;

/* Tie NC_I13 to ground at the package. */

Compile the listing for a GAL20V8-compatible target, then program and verify the PALCE20V8. Keep the compiler version and generated JEDEC checksum with the board build record.

U_IDE_SEQ is a CD74HCT164E. Tie serial inputs A and B high, connect MFP_CLK_5 to CLK, and connect IDE_CYCLE to active-low CLR. QB becomes high on the second rising clock edge after the PAL accepts a cycle. QD becomes high on the fourth edge. Ending the cycle drives CLR low and clears both taps without waiting for a clock.

PIO mode 0 timing produced by the adapter
Interval Adapter value PIO mode 0 minimum
Chip select and address before read/write strobe At least one 5 MHz period, less logic skew 70 ns
DIOR_n or DIOW_n before completion Two 5 MHz periods, about 400 ns 290 ns
Transfer cycle At least four 5 MHz periods plus CPU release 600 ns

The PAL holds IDE_DTACK_n high while IDE_IORDY is low. A 4.7 kohm pull-up at the motherboard receiver supplies the ready state for a device that does not drive the line. U_IDE_BUS, an SN74HCT244N, buffers DA2..DA0, both chip selects, both strobes, and reset onto the cable. The three address outputs also feed PAL inputs IDE_A3..IDE_A1 before their series resistors. Tie both output-enable pins low.

U_IDE_BUS channel assignment
Input pin and signal Output pin and signal
2, CPU A1 18, IDE_A1 / DA0
4, CPU A2 16, IDE_A2 / DA1
6, CPU A3 14, IDE_A3 / DA2
8, IDE_CS0_n 12, ATA CS0_n
11, IDE_CS1_n 9, ATA CS1_n
13, IDE_DIOR_n 7, ATA DIOR_n
15, IDE_DIOW_n 5, ATA DIOW_n
17, IDE_RESET_n 3, ATA RESET_n

Ground pins 1 and 19, connect pin 10 to ground, and connect pin 20 to +5 V. Place each source-series resistor after the listed output. Tap IDE_A1..IDE_A3 for the PAL before those resistors.

The CPU-side load added by IDE is one HCT244 input on each of A1..A3, one PAL input on A4, one PAL input on each data strobe, and one HCT04 input on R/W. Each data bit sees one HCT245 port. Include socket, route, and probe capacitance in the motherboard load audit.

On U_IDE_IRQ, gate 1 inverts processor R/W and gate 2 inverts it again to make IDE_RW. Gate 3 inverts ATA INTRQ to make IDE_IRQ_n. Ground the three unused inputs and leave their outputs open.

6. ATA Connector

J_IDE is a keyed, shrouded, 2-by-20, 2.54 mm header at the board edge. Remove pin 20 for the cable key and mark pin 1. The motherboard supplies signal ground through the cable. The drive power harness supplies +5 V and +12 V through the drive power connector.

40-pin parallel ATA host connector
Pin Signal Pin Signal
1 RESET_n 2 Ground
3 DD7 4 DD8
5 DD6 6 DD9
7 DD5 8 DD10
9 DD4 10 DD11
11 DD3 12 DD12
13 DD2 14 DD13
15 DD1 16 DD14
17 DD0 18 DD15
19 Ground 20 Key, pin absent
21 DMARQ, no receiver 22 Ground
23 DIOW_n 24 Ground
25 DIOR_n 26 Ground
27 IORDY 28 CSEL, ground at host
29 DMACK_n, 4.7 kohm pull-up 30 Ground
31 INTRQ 32 IOCS16_n, no receiver
33 DA1 34 PDIAG_n/CBLID_n, no host load
35 DA0 36 DA2
37 CS0_n 38 CS1_n
39 DASP_n, no host load 40 Ground

The host does not implement DMA. The pull-up holds DMACK_n inactive. Do not connect DMARQ or IOCS16_n to the processor bus. Device 0 and device 1 use PDIAG_n and DASP_n between themselves during startup, so the host adds no load to those pins.

7. Interrupt and Reset

ATA INTRQ drives one SN74HCT04N inverter. The inverter output, IDE_IRQ_n, drives U_IPL_ENC /I2. A 10 kohm pull-down holds the cable-side input inactive if no drive is connected. Processor level 2 uses autovector $1A. The interrupt handler reads the command block Status register to clear the device request. It reads Alternate Status when it must inspect status without clearing an interrupt.

U_IDE_RESET uses one half of a CD74HCT123E. Tie /A low and /CLR high, and drive B with PERIPH_RESET_n. The rising reset-release edge starts a nominal 4.5 ms pulse with a 100 kohm resistor and 100 nF capacitor. The complementary output is IDE_RESET_PULSE_n. The PAL combines the incoming reset and the pulse before U_IDE_BUS drives the cable. 

IDE_RESET_n = PERIPH_RESET_n AND IDE_RESET_PULSE_n

The direct term asserts reset without waiting for the monostable. The pulse term holds reset after release, so the 12.4 microsecond CPU RESET instruction produces a pulse longer than the ATA 25 microsecond minimum. The board's 100 ms power-on reset also reaches the drive. Firmware waits for both devices to finish diagnostics and leave BSY before issuing a command. Ground /CLR on the unused monostable half and fix both trigger inputs.

8. Firmware Rules

  1. Wait for BSY to clear after reset. Apply the ATA device-selection delays.
  2. Probe device 0 and device 1. Issue IDENTIFY DEVICE. If the device aborts it and reports an ATAPI signature, issue IDENTIFY PACKET DEVICE.
  3. Read capability words before choosing CHS, LBA28, LBA48, sector size, removable-media handling, or packet commands.
  4. Keep transfers in PIO mode 0. Do not enable multiword DMA or UDMA.
  5. Transfer the data register with 16-bit word accesses. Swap each sector-data word between the ATA port and byte-addressed big-endian memory.
  6. Use byte accesses for task-file and control registers. Poll BSY, DRQ, DF, and ERR at each command phase and impose a software timeout measured in milliseconds or seconds.
  7. Install an autovector level-2 handler before enabling ATA interrupts. Polling remains valid while nIEN is set in Device Control.

ATAPI support needs the PACKET command and the packet command set in firmware. The motherboard supplies the same register, interrupt, and data paths to ATA and ATAPI devices.

9. Parts and Wiring

IDE interface parts
Reference Part Function
U_IDE_CTRL PALCE20V8Q-15JC/4 Decode, strobes, wait gating, completion, and reset
U_IDE_SEQ CD74HCT164E 5 MHz transfer timing taps
U_IDE_RESET CD74HCT123E 4.5 ms reset-release stretcher
U_IDE_DATA_LO, U_IDE_DATA_HI 2 x SN74HCT245N 16-bit cable data isolation
U_IDE_BUS SN74HCT244N Address and control cable drivers
U_IDE_IRQ SN74HCT04N INTRQ inversion and two-stage R/W buffering; three gates unused
J_IDE Keyed 2-by-20, 2.54 mm shrouded header 40-pin host cable
RN_IDE_DATA 16 x 33 ohm series resistors Data-line source termination
RN_IDE_CTRL 8 x 33 ohm series resistors Address and control source termination

Fit one 100 nF ceramic capacitor at each IC supply pair and one 10 uF bulk capacitor near J_IDE. The IC families and packages predate the project's 1994 cutoff. The PAL uses a socketed PLCC; the remaining ICs use plastic DIP packages.

10. Layout

  • Put J_IDE at the board edge and keep the keyed cable clear of the expansion cards.
  • Put both HCT245 parts and the 33 ohm data resistors between the processor bus and the connector.
  • Put U_IDE_BUS and its series resistors beside the connector.
  • Keep each data route short and match the paths within the 16-bit group. Route a ground return beside the cable interface.
  • Keep IDE_IORDY and INTRQ away from clock traces. Place their pull resistors at the motherboard receivers.

11. Verification

Required checks
Check Pass condition
PAL build CUPL fits the equations and fixed pins in a PALCE20V8-compatible fuse map; programmer verification passes.
Idle bus Both chip selects, both strobes, and IDE_DTACK_n stay high with no slot-11 cycle.
PIO timing Measured address setup, strobe width, recovery, and cycle time meet PIO mode 0 at both cable connectors.
IORDY Holding IORDY low keeps the CPU waiting and keeps the active ATA strobe low until IORDY rises or the motherboard timeout expires.
Byte lanes Task-file byte accesses use D7..D0. Data-register word tests preserve all 16 bit positions and the BIOS byte swap preserves sector byte order.
Device combinations Device 0 alone, device 1 alone, and two devices enumerate with jumper and Cable Select configurations.
Media types One ATA disk, one ATAPI optical drive, a 44-pin disk through an adapter, and CompactFlash through a True IDE adapter complete repeated reads.
Interrupt INTRQ produces level 2, acknowledge produces autovector $1A, and a Status read clears the request.
Reset Power-on, push-button, watchdog, and CPU RESET assertion reach connector pin 1 with the required pulse width.
